subject: Made-to-measure alcove cabinetry
hook: Measure your alcove once and you'll get the wrong number.
ig:
Measure your alcove once and you'll get the wrong number.

Walls in older houses are rarely straight, and the difference shows up as a gap.

If you're thinking about alcove units this year, here's how we measure one:

Width at floor, middle and top. Use the narrowest.
Depth from the back wall to the front of the chimney breast.
Skirting, dado and picture rails: height and thickness.
Sockets, switches and nearby radiators.
Floor level across the opening.

Write it down on a quick sketch with the chimney breast drawn in. It helps you think about what you want there, whether that's cupboards below and shelves above, or full-height storage.

You don't need to get it perfect. We measure everything again at the survey before anything is made. But knowing your numbers makes the design conversation faster and more useful.

Save this for later and use the link in bio to see our made-to-measure alcove and living room furniture.
fb:
Got a pair of empty alcoves either side of the chimney breast? You're not alone. It's one of the most common spaces we're asked about in older homes around Staffordshire.

Before you think about styles, it's worth knowing your numbers. Measure the width at three heights (walls are rarely straight), the depth to the front of the chimney breast, any skirting or rails, sockets and radiators, and whether the floor is level.

We'll measure it all again properly at our free survey, but this gives you a head start. Swipe through and save it.

on_asset: S1: Measure your alcove once and you'll get it wrong | How a maker measures an alcove | S2: Width at three heights — Measure across at floor, middle and top. Old walls lean and bow, and the narrowest figure is the one that decides the unit. | S3: Depth to the chimney breast — Measure from the back wall to the front of the breast. It tells you how deep the unit can go before it sticks out past it. | S4: Find the skirting and rails — Note the height and thickness of skirting, dado or picture rails. The unit either scribes over them or they come off. | S5: Mark sockets and radiators — A socket in the alcove needs a cut-out or access; a radiator nearby affects where doors open. | S6: Check the floor for level — Lay a level across the alcove. A sloping floor means plinths or adjustable legs, planned now rather than packed later. | S7: Save this for your alcoves | Three widths, depth, skirting, sockets, level.
